context: A uni student interviews a retired entertainer about radio shows
purpose: Teach: ロケット/対決/ゾーン/ビッグ/スタンス/リクエスト/駆使/パチンコ

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間ありがとうございます。早速ですが、深夜ラジオの黄金時代って、本当にビッグなスターが何人もいらっしゃいましたよね。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. To get right to it, the golden age of late-night radio really had so many big stars, didn't it?
lines.style: Polite student opener, slightly nervous but eager researcher tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、そうだなあ。あの頃は本当にすごかったよ。番組同士の聴取率対決なんて、毎週ロケットみたいに数字が上がったり下がったりしてな。
lines.en: Ah, yes indeed. Those days were really something. The ratings battles between shows went up and down like a rocket every single week.
lines.style: Warm reminiscing elder, slow nostalgic cadence with chuckles.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ロケットみたいに、ですか。当時のリスナーからのリクエスト曲って、どんなふうに選ばれていたんですか？
lines.en: Like a rocket, you say. How were the listener request songs actually chosen back then?
lines.style: Curious follow-up question, leaning forward attentively as interviewer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ハガキを山ほど読んでな、自分の感覚を駆使して選ぶんだ。マイクの前に座ると、不思議とゾーンに入る感じでね。
lines.en: We'd read mountains of postcards and use all our instincts to choose them. Once you sat in front of the mic, you'd strangely enter the zone.
lines.style: Confident craftsman pride, hands gesturing as he describes.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ゾーンに入る、っていう感覚、すごく分かる気がします。ちなみに、スポンサーとの関係で何か気を遣うこととかあったんでしょうか？
lines.en: I think I really understand that 'in the zone' feeling. By the way, were there things you had to be careful about with sponsors?
lines.style: Empathetic agreement then shifting to sharper journalistic angle.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そりゃあったよ。特にパチンコ業界がスポンサーだった時期は、発言のスタンスを慎重にしないといけなかった。
lines.en: Of course there were. Especially when the pachinko industry was our sponsor, we had to keep a careful stance on our remarks.
lines.style: Candid older man lowering voice, conspiratorial honesty.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: スタンスを意識して話すって、相当神経使いますよね。最後に、若い放送作家志望に何かアドバイスをいただけますか？
lines.en: Being conscious of your stance while speaking must take real mental effort. Finally, could you give any advice to aspiring young broadcasters?
lines.style: Respectful wrap-up, notebook closing, sincere closing question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: とにかく自分の言葉を持つこと。技術を駆使するのも大事だが、結局はリスナーと一対一の真剣勝負だからな。
lines.en: Above all, have your own words. Using technique matters too, but in the end it's a serious one-on-one match with the listener.
lines.style: Heartfelt mentor wisdom, slow deliberate delivery with weight.
